correctness_confidence.basis: The original adversarial review found no material defect under the stated hypotheses after examining the uniform reduction, coherent states, infinite-dimensional entropy arguments, atomic singularity, parameter coverage, both energy constraints, global certificates, thermal gap and endpoint laws. This is model review, not formal certification or a numerical probability of correctness.

rigor.basis: Theorems 2.1 and 3.1 are supported by finite-label conditional-entropy control, Gibbs relative entropy and global discrete inequalities; feasibility and the order of limits are addressed. Two short derivations could be made more explicit, but the original review did not find a missing material premise.

novelty.basis: The probable advance is the uniform reduction and explicit fixed-energy-ratio minimax constant curve, including atomic and diffuse constructions, thermal-adversary separation and endpoint laws. The identity/replacement channel family, binary-branch mechanism and plateau constant have antecedents. Priority is not certified: the search was directed, and Baitenov (2024) was accessible only through its primary editorial abstract.

significance.basis: A substantive specialized solution of an adversarial reset problem, potentially useful as an exact reference case. It does not determine regularized quantum capacity, finite-energy exact capacity, general attenuator behavior or efficient universal codes, and there is no evidence here of field-wide impact or Millennium-level significance.

reproducibility.basis: The original review replayed 28/28 corrected finite cases on Windows with Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.2.6 and SciPy 1.18.0; maximum constraint residual was 3.675e-14 and reset LP gap 4.181e-11. The failed initial solver case was preserved separately. Additional checks covered 120 complex-state pairs and 30 continuum profiles. These are floating-point checks, not proofs; six large-energy continuum cases, Linux, internal audits and CI were not newly reproduced.

summary: This is a schema conversion of the closed private review 53 and its bibliographic addendum for the identical PDF, not a second evaluation or a new fresh-context scientific review. The original review was initiated as a fresh-context task; this follow-up retains that review and only formats its findings. The requested configuration was OpenAI gpt-6-astra with xhigh effort. The model family had participated in mathematical checks during manuscript development; the filesystem was shared, with no claim of technical isolation or external runtime attestation. The original review identified no material mathematical defect and recommended specialized publication with nonblocking expository suggestions. It rated quality 5.5/10 and AIRR importance 4.5/10 separately; both ratings are unchanged. Here millennium_score represents the 4.5 importance rating, and overall_stars=5 is its nearest-integer display, not a new score or the rounded quality rating. The most valuable contribution is the uniform quantum-to-classical reduction together with an explicit fixed-ratio minimax loss curve and global discrete certificates. The plateau constant and the channel family are already known. The recommendation remains favorable, represented as accept, without claiming an editorial decision. assessed_at records the original package closure timestamp; ARR-ASSESS-1.0 identifies this representation schema. The original manuscript source was read in full; cited literature was read to the explicitly recorded scope, and Baitenov's full text was unavailable. The finite computations corroborate selected cases and do not establish the infinite-limit theorems or exhaustive priority.
strengths: Theorem 2.1 gives a reduction uniform over finite reset budgets, including changing adversaries, coherent states and the infinite-dimensional oscillator setting; dephasing is justified through finite-label continuity rather than an unsupported entropy-continuity assertion.

Theorem 3.1 and Lemmas 3.2–3.3 combine explicit atomic and diffuse profiles with full-support relative-entropy certificates and feasible discrete approximations. The proof retains both input and reset energy bounds.

The consequences include the vanishing-deficit criterion M=o(E), the fixed-ratio curve and plateau, and a strict asymptotic gap for thermal reset adversaries when 0<c<1. The two endpoint laws were checked separately in the original review.

The original investigation distinguished an initial solver success flag from a valid saddle certificate, retained the failed historical case, and separated finite numerical checks from the analytical proof.
weaknesses: Nonblocking exposition suggestion A: in Section 5, pages 7–8, before S1 and the connection used in S4, explicitly evaluate the mixed-measure saddle functional as Ψ(f,t*)=2λ ln[B_z(s,3/2)/b]+(q−2λs)ln z+b(2λs−qc), retaining the atomic contribution −qw ln q. This is a short algebraic clarification, not a repair of a theorem.

Nonblocking exposition suggestion B: at the end of Section 3.1, page 4, show the substitution r=sy and exponential domination of scaled moments in the limit z decreasing to q. State that λ is fixed in (0,1); the review does not claim uniform endpoint control in λ.

Bibliographic suggestion from the original addendum: cite Giovannetti–Lloyd–Ruskai, quant-ph/0408103v3, Section IV.B, equation (34), for the finite-dimensional identity/replacement family with arbitrary fixed replacement state. Its output-norm multiplicativity question differs from the present energy-constrained entanglement-assisted minimax problem.

The full text of Baitenov, On Jensen Gap and Capacity of a Shifted Depolarizing Quantum Channel (2024), could not be obtained. Its editorial abstract describes a one-shot capacity and two optimal-ensemble regimes. Detailed overlap remains unverified; this limits novelty confidence without establishing a material mathematical objection.

The claim is specialized and asymptotic. The review does not establish a general Gaussian-extremality counterexample, an attenuator result, uniqueness of all optimal sequences, efficient coding or a broad operational universality theorem. Literature access was selective, the search was not exhaustive, and no external runtime attestation, human review or formal proof certificate is supplied.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 2.1: a uniform high-energy reduction of the adversarial entanglement-assisted reset problem to a diagonal entropy game, with a correction independent of the finite reset budget.
Theorem 3.1 and Lemmas 3.2–3.3: the explicit constant-loss curve at every fixed positive energy ratio, its atomic/diffuse profile structure, and global discrete certificates that retain feasibility.
Section 5: strict separation of thermal reset adversaries for 0<c<1 and the square-root and quadratic endpoint laws, subject to the prior-art search and access limits stated above.
